Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

due to preposition

also because of, owing to, on account of, thanks to, thanks to me, thanks to you

classical

Caes. BG 1.16.2: nam propter frīgora … nōn modo frūmenta in agrīs mātūra nōn erant
Cic. Att. 7.5.2: propter hūmānitātem et modestiam mālō salvum quam propter ūsum meum

propter (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

because of, due to, on account of

The plain word for a cause, and the chief sense of propter (Lewis & Short). With persons, “because of me, thanks to you”: propter mē, propter tē.

Other words

  • ob (+ accusative) — because of, for (a reason, a deed)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 978–978b: Ob eam rem? — Ob eam.; Cic. Rep. 1.12: ob eam causam (Lewis & Short)

    Mostly in set phrases: ob eam rem, for that reason; quam ob rem, which is why.

  • prae (+ ablative) — for, because of (something that prevents)

    preposition with the ablative, with a negative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.12.1: prae lacrimīs possum reliqua nec cōgitāre nec scrībere

    Classically only of a hindrance, with a negative or vix (Lewis & Short): one cannot speak for tears, see for the crowd.

  • operā + gen. — thanks to, through (someone’s doing)

    the ablative of opera, with a genitive or a possessive (meā, tuā operā) · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 11: meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī; Ter. Hec. 228: nōn meā operā neque pol culpā ēvēnit

    “Thanks to me”, “through my doing”, for good or ill (Lewis & Short).

  • meā (tuā) operā — thanks to me (you), through my (your) doing

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 11: meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī; Traupman 393

    The possessive in the ablative with operā, “by my effort”: Latin says whose work it was, not whom one should thank.

Examples

  • nam propter frīgora … nōn modo frūmenta in agrīs mātūra nōn erant

    for due to the cold … the corn in the fields was not even ripeCaes. BG 1.16.2

  • Ut propter mē tibi sit melius mihique propter tē et tuōs.

    So that you may be better off thanks to me, and I thanks to you and yours.Plaut. Aul. 225

  • prae lacrimīs possum reliqua nec cōgitāre nec scrībere

    for tears I can neither think nor write the restCic. Att. 9.12.1

  • glōriantī atque ita dīcentī, ‘meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī,’ ‘certē,’ inquit rīdēns, ‘nam nisi tū āmīsissēs, numquam recēpissem.’

    when the man boasted, “Thanks to me, Quintus Fabius, you recovered Tarentum,” Fabius laughed and said, “Certainly: if you hadn’t lost it, I should never have recovered it.”Cic. Sen. 11

See also why, therefore, by, for.
